chunks: And by this chain, from Al-Minqari, from Abdul Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

I saw all goodness gathered in cutting off greed for what is in the hands of people; and whoever does not hope in people for anything and refers his matter to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his affairs, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will answer him in everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the key to receiving all goodness and having one's needs answered by God according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual principle of 'qat' al-tama'' (cutting off hope/desire for people), a cornerstone of Shia asceticism that fosters complete reliance on God. By redirecting one's expectations from created beings to the Creator, the believer achieves a state of divine responsiveness where Allah answers their needs comprehensively. This teaching underscores the transition from social dependency to spiritual self-sufficiency, a key theme in the chapter on 'self-sufficiency from the people'.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Minqary, from Abdul Razzaq, from Moamar, from Al Zahry, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> saw the goodness, all of it having gathered in cutting off the greed from what is in the hands of the people; and the one who does not hope to the people regarding anything and refers his matter to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic in the entirety of his matters, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Answer to him with regards to everything’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from al-Minqari from ‘Abd al- Razzaq from Mu’ammar from al-Zuhri from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

I saw all good gathered together in cutting off of yearning for what belongs to people and in not having any hope in people in anything and in leaving his affairs in the hands of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, in all matters. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will answer him in all things.”
